articles.excerpt: This is the second part of the series "Your first steps in Computer Vision on AWS". If you are just starting, this tutorial will guide you step by step from the initial dataset to a deployed app. You…
articles.body: This is the second part of the series "Your first steps in Computer Vision on AWS". If you are just starting, this tutorial will guide you step by step from the initial dataset to a deployed app. You can read the first part on ASL dataset + preprocessing . Why training on CPU would take ages While we used a simple CPU SageMaker notebook instance to work with the data, for training we would need a GPU-powered instance. A CPU is designed for complex sequential tasks. Training a CNN requires performing millions of simple matrix multiplications and convolutions simultaneously. A GPU contains thousands of smaller, simpler cores designed to execute thousands of calculations at the exact same time, offering massive parallelism.

articles.title: When the engine's phoneme and the course IPA disagree
articles.excerpt: A user said our IPA for "cause" was wrong. We almost changed the lexicon. We run an English speaking-practice app. After someone records a word, we show a score from Azure Pronunciation Assessment and…
articles.body: A user said our IPA for "cause" was wrong. We almost changed the lexicon. We run an English speaking-practice app. After someone records a word, we show a score from Azure Pronunciation Assessment and a drawer of phonemes: the sound the course expects, a short hint in Chinese, and how close that attempt was. They hit cause . Our course IPA is /kɑːz/: an open, unrounded "ah." The drawer marked /ɔ/ and explained it as a rounded "oh." Both symbols sat on the same screen. If you are learning, that looks like the app cannot agree with itself. First wrong fix: change the lexicon Did we store the wrong American IPA for cause ? Plenty of dictionaries still print /kɔːz/. Our teaching accent is General American with the cot–caught merger, so law , thought , caught , and cause all go to ɑː.

articles.title: vLLM vs TGI vs Ollama: GPU Memory Throughput, PagedAttention & Batching Benchmarks
articles.excerpt: vLLM vs TGI vs Ollama: GPU Memory Throughput, PagedAttention & Batching Benchmarks 1. Executive Summary & Decision Matrix All three systems serve LLM inference, but they occupy non-overlapping points…
articles.body: vLLM vs TGI vs Ollama: GPU Memory Throughput, PagedAttention & Batching Benchmarks 1. Executive Summary & Decision Matrix All three systems serve LLM inference, but they occupy non-overlapping points on the production spectrum. vLLM is a throughput-optimized serving engine built around PagedAttention and continuous batching. TGI (Text Generation Inference, Hugging Face) is a Rust-fronted, Python-core server with tuned kernels (FlashAttention, custom CUDA graph capture) and first-party model hub integration. Ollama is a llama.cpp-based local runner — GGUF quantized models, CPU/hybrid execution, zero-ops — and it is not designed for concurrent serving at all.

articles.title: Your AI Coding Agent Wrote It — Now Who Reviews It? The Rise of AI-Assisted Code Review
articles.excerpt: Originally published on tamiz.pro. AI coding agents like GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Devin have crossed a threshold: they no longer autocomplete snippets, they implement entire features. A 2024 GitHub…
articles.body: Originally published on tamiz.pro . AI coding agents like GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Devin have crossed a threshold: they no longer autocomplete snippets, they implement entire features. A 2024 GitHub survey found that 92% of U.S. developers already use AI coding tools, and the median share of AI-generated code in active repositories is climbing steadily. The result is a quiet but profound shift in engineering culture: the bottleneck is no longer writing code — it's reviewing it. When a human writes code, the reviewer's job is to catch mistakes, enforce style, and challenge design decisions.

articles.body: Moderator bias in usability testing occurs when a facilitator's tone, body language, facial expressions, or follow-up questions inadvertently steer participants toward giving favorable feedback. Quick solution: Use a standardized, non-leading script and neutral prompts for every session, as outlined in official guidance on conducting qualitative usability testing studies . moderation_mode : " neutral" script_version : " v2.4" validation_check : " strict" Prerequisites include reviewing standard protocols and ensuring that observers understand how to record facts separately from interpretations. Be cautious not to rely on ad-hoc prompts, which often introduce subtle coaching.

articles.title: My Terminal Is Haunted by a Programmer Who Never Finished Their Deploy
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine haunted-shell possesses your zsh. A ghost lives in the terminal: the programmer who died at this keyboa…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built haunted-shell possesses your zsh. A ghost lives in the terminal: the programmer who died at this keyboard years ago, with a deploy still unfinished. It watches every command you run, and sometimes, in dim violet italics that type themselves out a little too slowly, it whispers back. $ git push --force origin main your git push failed, but i'm sure you knew that. the main branch is still here, waiting for you. $ rm -rf node_modules i watched you delete the node_modules. you're so reckless. i once tried to save them. now they're gone. $ npm run build the build failed. you're still using node 12. i never got to fix that bug. It never helps you, by design.

articles.title: The Taurid meteor shower isn't much to look at. That's why I love it
articles.excerpt: The Taurids produce only a handful of meteors an hour. That sounds disappointing, but I've learned that expecting almost nothing can make this one of the most enjoyable meteor showers of the year.
articles.body: I used to make a basic mistake with meteor showers — I treated the zenith hourly rate (ZHR) like a timetable. If a shower were advertised at 20 meteors per hour, I'd go outside expecting something roughly every three minutes. After 10 quiet minutes, I'd start wondering what I was doing wrong. After half an hour, I'd start to doubt the whole idea of meteor showers . The Northern and Southern Taurids cured me of all that. Two linked meteor showers that peak around Nov. 4-5 and Nov. 11-12 this year, they each manage only about five meteors per hour under ideal conditions. In reality, you may see fewer. You may spend a long time seeing none. So what's the point?

articles.body: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI) Intricate structures within the Cat’s Head Nebula are illuminated in this mid-infrared view from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Oct. 29, 2026. The distinctive “cat’s head” shape of the nebula was likely sculpted over time by the intense ultraviolet radiation and winds from massive stars in the Carina Nebula. As this stellar feedback erodes the surrounding gas and dust, denser material within the feline-shaped pillar resists erosion, at least for now.
